questions.q: According to this lesson, what mistake is a security architect making by committing to one specific framework before understanding the organization?
options: The same mistake SABSA warns against — choosing a control, or here a framework, before it's tied to a real requirement
No mistake at all, since every framework produces identical results regardless of organizational context
Violating a TOGAF rule that requires written approval from The Open Group before any framework is selected
Breaking a CISA regulation that mandates ZTMM as the only acceptable architecture framework
questions.explain: Committing to a framework before understanding the organization repeats SABSA's core warning: a control, or a framework choice, that isn't tied to a real requirement isn't architecture — it's just a preference.

questions.q: Why is SABSA-style traceability often the most valuable thing to introduce for a regulated organization facing a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audit?
options: Because auditors only accept SABSA-certified architects as valid witnesses
Because SOC 2 and ISO 27001 explicitly require the full six-layer SABSA Matrix to be completed
Because an auditor will ask exactly the "why does this control exist" question that SABSA's traceability discipline is built to answer
Because SABSA is the only framework that satisfies PCI DSS requirements
questions.explain: Auditors routinely ask why a given control exists and what it's meant to achieve — precisely the question SABSA's business-traceability discipline is designed to answer clearly.

questions.q: What is the "outer process, inner content" blending pattern described in this lesson?
options: Running SABSA only for external audits and TOGAF only for internal projects, never together
Running TOGAF's ADM for governance and cadence while organizing the security work inside it using SABSA's layers and traceability
Replacing TOGAF entirely with ZTMM once an organization reaches Optimal maturity on all five pillars
Using ZTMM as the sole top-level framework for the entire enterprise architecture practice
questions.explain: In this pattern, TOGAF's ADM supplies the outer process and governance cadence, while SABSA's layers and Business Attributes Profile supply the business-traceable security content inside each phase.

questions.q: What does a "lightweight SABSA subset" look like for many mid-size organizations, per this lesson?
options: A fully staffed SABSA Institute certification program for every employee
Running the complete 36-cell SABSA Matrix for every single security control, with no exceptions
Adopting only the Business Attributes Profile and the traceability habit — can you point to the business reason for this control — without the full six-layer matrix
Skipping SABSA entirely in favor of a homegrown, uncodified process
questions.explain: Many mid-size companies capture most of SABSA's real value by adopting just the Business Attributes Profile and the discipline of traceability, without running the full six-layer matrix formally.

questions.q: What is the central, practical takeaway this lesson gives for adapting a framework to a real organization?
options: Always implement every layer of SABSA and every phase of TOGAF exactly as published, regardless of organization size
Pick whichever framework the most recent industry conference promoted most heavily
Avoid using more than one framework under any circumstances, since blending always creates conflicting governance
Take the artifacts that solve a real, present problem and leave the rest, matching depth to the organization's actual size, maturity, and driver
questions.explain: The lesson's core guidance is to adapt rather than implement by the book — using the parts of a framework that solve a real, present problem, scaled to the organization's actual size, maturity, and driver, rather than applying any framework uniformly.
